resolvedFinding.reason: Both linked blocks now explicitly use the settled-current one-dimensional thin-wire approximation, constant carrier density and resistivity, and neglect of appreciable curvature/contact redistribution. Shape independence is approximate and restricted to the model's range; drift is averaged and the field is longitudinal and averaged. The text expressly rejects strict equality of the real local field at all points of a bent conductor. These qualifications remove the original overclaim without changing its source or mathematical tokens.

shapeQualification.independentReason: The old arbitrary-angle claim is replaced by bending only within an explicitly stated thin-wire one-dimensional approximation, with appreciable bending and contact redistribution neglected. Constant carrier density and resistivity are declared, while material, length, section, temperature and supply conditions are held fixed. The added acute-bend exclusion prevents treating curvature effects as universally negligible.

currentQualification.independentReason: In that model R is approximately rho*L/S. Unchanged rho, L, S and supply conditions therefore support approximate shape independence of settled current, not exact shape independence in a finite bend. The explicit settled-current scope excludes the coil's switch-on inductive transient. These are reviewer arguments, not added lesson formulas.

driftQualification.independentReason: For unchanged cross-section S and uniform carrier density n, fixed total current fixes the cross-section-averaged longitudinal drift magnitude |I|/(n*|q0|*S); it does not fix every carrier's local drift in a curved section. The revised wording names average directed speed, keeps n fixed and places the claim inside the linked one-dimensional model. Its equality concerns the averaged quantity, not pointwise uniformity.

fieldQualification.independentReason: Within the original ordinary ohmic-conduction model at fixed rho, the longitudinal field is approximately rho*I/S in the one-dimensional limit. The revised text states approximately equal averaged longitudinal magnitudes, retains the curvature/contact exclusions and explicitly denies strict equality of local fields throughout a real bent conductor. Its final sentence scopes the field-line description to the same approximation; this is text assessment only, not approval of figure169.

oldCounterexampleDisposition.independentReason: The original finite toroidal bend still has E_theta and J_theta proportional to 1/r, nonuniform local drift and an exact resistance differing from that of a straight wire of the same centreline length and section. The correction does not deny any of this. When the section radius a is small relative to centreline radius R0 and curvature/contact effects are neglected, r is approximately R0 across a section, recovering the leading one-dimensional current and field description. Thus the old counterexample refutes the unchanged historical wording but no longer refutes the expressly approximate current wording.
